FOREWORD

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 28 May 1987, after the draft finalized by the Pest Control Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council and the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 FenvaIerate, technical is used for the formulation meant for (he \ control of agricultural pests. 0.3 Fenvalerate is the ,accepted common name by the International Organization for Standardization ( IS0 ) for ( RS )-h-cyano, J-phenoxybenzyl ( RS ) 2-( 4-chlorophenyl ) 3-methylbutyrate. Its empirical and structural formulae and the molecular mass are given below: Empirical Formula C2,H&IN02 Structural Formula Mvlccular Mass 419.9

0.4 In the preparation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of the Insecticides Act, 1968 and the Rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under the Act and Rules, wherever applicable. 0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed, or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of' the specifird value in this standard. *Rules for rounding off numerical values ( rev&i

NOTE - The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated bv the producer., Standard marked products are also continuously checked bv BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers, may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 4.

shall be the high performance liquid chromatography ( HPLC ) method ( see A-l ) or GLC method ( see A-2 ). A p a r t f r o m t h e s e m e t h o d , . ultraviolet ( UV ) spectrophotometric method ( see A-3 ) may be followed as a routine method. At frequent intervals, the HPLC or GLC assay shall be conducted to check the values obtained by the routine methods.
N OTE -The checking through the UV method should cover batch to batch variation, while the HPLC or GLC method should cover the variation in technical material used for making formulations.

A-l. HIGH PERFORMANCE LIQUID CHROMATOGRAPHIC METHOD
assay. Using solutions containing known amounts of the standard fenvalerate sample and the internal standard ( Is ), the response .factor ( R ) for fenvalerate in the internal standard approach is arrived at. A solution containing known mass of the fenvalerate sample ( under investigation ) and internal standard is injected subsequently. The percentage of fenvalerate in the sample is then computed by the standard relationship. A-1.2 A p p a r a t u s

A-1.2.2 Volumetric Flask - 50-ml and IOO-ml capacity.
A-1.2.3 Pipettes ( graduated ) - 2-ml, 5-ml and IO-ml capacity. A-l.3 Reagents A-1.3.1 Di-n-butyl Phtbalate - AR Grade ( Internal standard ). A-1.3.2 Carbon Tetrarhloride - Spectioscopic grade. A-1.3.3 Chloroform - Spectroscopic grade. A-1.3.4 Standard Fenvaierate - Of known purity (Minimum 92 percent ). A-1.4 Preparation of Standard Solution atid Calculations of R F and Percentage Fenvalerate A-1.4.1 Preparation of Internal Standard ( Is ) Solution - Weigh accurately 1.0 g of Di-n-butyl phthalate ( DBP ) ( Is ) into loo-ml volumetric flask. Dilute it up to the volume with carbon tetrachloride-chloroform ( 85 : 15, v/v ) mixture. This gives 10 mg/ml of DBP solution. A-1.4.2 Preparation of Standard Fenvalerate Solution for Response Factor ( R F ) - weigh accurately 8'1 g of standard fenvalerate of known purity into lOO-ml volumetric flask. Add 10 ml of `Is' solution and dilute up to the mark w-ith solvent system. This solution gives 1 000 ppm of fenvalerate and DBP.
l

A-1.4.3 Introduce 10 ~1 of this solution to the HPLC and _Yom the chromatogram calculate response factor as follows: Response factor ( Rf ) = -$-x where -Al = area of the fenvalerate, m, - concentration of di-n-butyl phthalate, A2 = area of di-n-butyl phthalate, and m2 = concentration of fenvalerate. A-l.5 Procedure A-1.5.1 Weigh 0.5 g of fenvalerate technical sample into IOO-ml volumetric flask. Make up to the volume with carbon tetrachloridechloroform mixture. Pipette out 10 ml of the s o l u t i o n into 50-ml volumetric flask. Then pipette out 5 ml of `Is' solution in the same flask. Mix well. Make up to the mark using the solvent system. A-1.5.2 Introduce 10 J.J of the above solution to the HPLC and, from chromatogram, calculate percentage purity of fenvalerate technical. 7
f$

A, = area of the fenvalerate peak in the sample taken for test, ml = mass of `Is' added, P = purity of the standard,

A2 = area of the `Is' peak, m2 = mass of the sample, and R f = responses factor. A-l.7 @recision - Data obtained by this method indicate a standard deviation of 0.70 for fenvalerate at 92 percent: level. A-2. GA S CHROMATOGRAPHIC METHOD

A-2.1.2 Volumetric Flask - 50-ml and loo-ml capacity. A-2.1.3 Separating Funnel - loo-ml capacity.
A-2.1.4 Microsyringe - 10 ~1 syringe with a needle of sufficient length to introduce the sample close to the top of the column packing. A-2.2 Reagents A-2.2.1 Standard Fenvalerate - minimum-92 percent ( m/m ).. A-2.2.2 Di ( 2-ethylhexyl ) Phthalate ( DBP ) - AR grade. A-2.2.3 Chloroform - Spectroscopic grade. A-2.3 Procedure A-2.3.1 Preparation of Internal Standard Solution ( Is ) - Weigh accurately 0'5 g DBP and dissolve in chloroform so as to make 1 litre of the solution. A-2.3.2 Preparation of Standard Fenvalerate Solution - Weigh accurately 0'075 g of standard fenvalerate in a beaker and add 2'5 ml of `Is' solution. Shake well to dissolve the fenvalerate. Transfer carefully into 50-ml volumetric flask using the `Is' and then make up to the mark. A-2.3.3 Preparation of Sample Solution - Weigh accurately about O-075 g of fenvalerate into a 50-ml volumetric flask and make up its volume with Is. A-2.3.4 Estimation - Inject 1 ~1 of standard fenvalerate solution ( see A-2.3.2 ) and sample under test ( see A-2.3.3 ). Measure the areas of fenvalerate and `Is' peaks in each case and compute the fenvalerate content. A-2.4 Calculation ml x Al x A3 x p Fenvalerate content, percent by mass = ~ m2 x A2 x A4 where m, - mass in g of the standard fenvalerate, m2 = mass in g of the sample taken for the test, A1 = area of internal standard peak in standard solution, & = area of internal standard peak in sample solution, A3 = area of fenvalerate peak in sample solution, A4 = area of internal standard peak in standard solution, and p = percentage purity of standard fenvalerate.
N OTE 1 - Peak area difference between the peaks of the standard of the sample and the internal standard should not be too large and response factor should be checked with every set of analysis.

18 : 12903 - 1987
N OTE 2 - Operational conditions and the indicated columti details are suggestive and could be varied depending on GLC, provided standardization is done. In case, separation of diastereo isomers of fenvalerate is observed, peak areas of these isomers be integrated and total fenvalerate content calculated.

A-3 ULTRAVIO&JJT

SPECTROPHOTOMETRIC METHOD

A-3.1 Prlnc3ple - The absorbance of a Qolution of the fenvalerate sample in carbon tetrachloride is measured at 278 nm against carbon ~tetrachloride blank. -The fenvalerate content of the sample is &en computed making use of a calibration graph prepared earlier ( tising a standard fenvalerate sample ). A-3.2 ,Apparatus A-3.2.1 Ultravidlet SpcGtrophotomcter A-3,2.2 Quartz Cells - Matched with path length equal to I*000 cm. A-3.2.3 Volumetric Flasks - loo-ml and 5&ml capacity. A-3.2.4 Pifette - 5-ml and lo-ml capacity ( gradutated ). A-3.3 Reagents A-3.3.1 Carbon Tetrachloride - Spectroscopic grade.
NOTE - The absorbance of this solvent should not exceed 1.000, O*lOO and PO05 at 263, 275 and 300 nm, respectively.

A-3.4 Procedure - Weigh actirately about 100 mg of standard fenvalerate sample into a loo-ml volumetric flask. Dissolve it in carbon tetrachioride and make up to volume. Pipette out 3.0, 4.0, 5.0 and 6'0 ml of this stock solution into four 50-ml volumetric flasks. Dilute them to the mark with carbon tetrachloride to obtain standard solutions of around 60, 80, 100 and 120 ppm respectively. Fill both the quartz cells with carbon tetrachloride and ensure that the cell error is insignificant ( about 0.001 ) at 278 nm. Obtain the absorbance of the four stand&d solutions referred to above, at 278 nm against carbon tetrach!oride blank. Use cells with lids to eliminate evaporation of carbon tetrachloride. Construct a calibration graph connecting absorbance values ( corrected for cell error, if any ) and concentrations of fenvalerate ( ins ppm ) in the standard solutions. Measure the slope ( S ) of the calibration graph. weigh t,ccurately about 100 mg of the fenvalerate sample under investigation mto a IOO-ml volumetric flask. Dissolve it in carbon tetrachloride and make up to volume. Pipette out 5'0 ml of this solution into a 50-ml volumetric flask. Dilute it to the mark with carbon tetrachloride to obtain a solution of around 100 ppm. Measure the absorbance of this solution at 278 nm against carbon tetrachloride blank. Compute the fenvalerate content .of the sample making use of the calibration graph. 10

A-3.3.2 Standard Fenvalerate - Of known .purity.

IS : 12003 - 1987

Ai3.5 Calculation 100 x A Fenvalerate content = M x S where A = absorbance of fenvalerate at 278 nm, M = mass of the fenvalerate sample in mg taken for analysis, and S = slope of the calibration graph. A-3.6 Precision - Data obtained by this method indicate a standard deviation of 0.6 for fenvalerate at 99 percent level.

B-3. PREPARATION' OF STANDARDS AND CALIBRATION B-3.1 Weigh out accurately 2.5 g of di-n-butyl phthalate into a 50-ml volumetric flask and make up to volume with chloroform. This will give a solution containing 50 mglml of metaphenoxy benzaldehyde. Pipette out 1'0, 2'0, 3'0, 4'0 and 5'0 ml of this metaphenoxy benzaldehyde solution into a clean dry lo-mltlask.
